heading: Before the tapes
lede: Isolated talks at Jain and all-religions gatherings from 1954, centred on Jabalpur. By 1962 he is touring central India and holding his first meditation camps. Most of these talks have no title, and the rows below name them by town.

photo.alt: White marble cliffs rising from the Narmada river
photo.caption: The Marble Rocks on the Narmada near Jabalpur, his base throughout these years.
photo.author: Anshikasjv12

label: 1954 to 1963

heading: The first camp at Ranakpur
lede: The year opens with private talks in Bombay in April. In June he holds his first meditation camp, at Muchala Mahavira near Ranakpur, later published as Sadhana Path. Sources place the first tape recording at this camp, though the wiki lists no surviving media for its talks.

photo.alt: A wide marble temple with many spires above a flight of steps
photo.caption: The Jain temple at Ranakpur. The camp was held nearby, at Muchala Mahavira.
photo.author: Ingo Mehling

heading: Mahabaleshwar, Udaipur and Saurashtra
lede: A camp at Mahabaleshwar in February gives Dhyan-Sutra, and a second camp follows at Udaipur in May. July is a tour of Saurashtra. The year closes with Jeevan Ki Khoj in Bombay.

photo.alt: A forested valley under low cloud
photo.caption: A valley at Mahabaleshwar, where the Dhyan-Sutra camp was held in February.
photo.author: Shiivamsharma

heading: Six camps in one year
lede: Camps run from Tulsishyam in February to Chikhaldara in December, by way of Udaipur, Bodh Gaya, Matheran and Nashik. Between them come long runs of talks at colleges in Poona and halls in Bombay.

photo.alt: Carved stone wall with three seated Buddha figures in niches
photo.caption: South wall of the Mahabodhi Temple at Bodh Gaya. The June camp was held in the town, at Samanway Ashram.
photo.author: Sumitsurai

heading: On the road all year
lede: The longest list so far. Camps at Udaipur, Matheran and Malad, a run of series in Hyderabad and Bombay, and tours through Gujarat, Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh, with Jabalpur talks threaded through the whole year.

photo.alt: A narrow road winding along a dry hillside seen from above
photo.caption: The view from Panorama Point, Matheran, site of the Asambhav Kranti camp in October.
photo.author: Dinesh Valke

heading: Camps and constant travel
lede: He returns to Jabalpur between tours through Gujarat, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Punjab, Delhi, Patna and Varanasi. Camps are listed at Ajol, Mandu, Nargol, Junagadh and Udaipur, and Sambhog Se Samadhi Ki Or is given in Bombay in August and September.

heading: Kashmir and the first English
lede: Tours take in Gujarat, Bombay, Punjab, Patna, Jamshedpur and Madras, with camps at Baroda, Junagadh, Matheran, Ahmedabad and Dwarka. In September he speaks on Mahavir at Srinagar and Pahalgam. The first rows the wiki marks as English appear this year, at Udaipur in June and at Pahalgam around 1 October.

heading: The move to Bombay
lede: Long runs of talks at CCI Chambers in Bombay, and a move to Woodland Apartments on 8 December. Camps are listed at Poona, Rajkot, Nargol, Baroda, Ajol, Manali and Ahmedabad. English interviews begin on 6 May.

heading: Bombay and the Mount Abu camps
lede: Based in Bombay, speaking at Woodlands, Cross Maidan and Patkar Hall. Geeta-Darshan continues, and Tao Upanishad and Mahaveer-Vani begin. Camps are held at Mount Abu in April and again in September and October. English talks run from January, typed on the wiki as interviews.

photo.alt: A lake ringed by wooded hills
photo.caption: Nakki Lake at Mount Abu, site of the camps of 1971 to 1974.
photo.author: Sanyam Bahga

heading: Upanishad camps, English series
lede: Based in Bombay. Three camps mix Hindi and English: Matheran in January, and Mount Abu in March and October. English series at Woodlands include The Ultimate Alchemy and, from 1 October, Vigyan Bhairav Tantra.

heading: Tantra, Tao and Mount Abu
lede: Based at Woodlands in Bombay. Vigyan Bhairav Tantra is completed in English, and Yoga The Alpha and Omega begins on 25 December. Camps are held at Anand Shila in February and three times at Mount Abu.

heading: From Bombay to Poona
lede: The year opens at Woodlands and with a January camp at Mount Abu. On 21 March he moves to Koregaon Park, Poona. The first Poona talks listed are Geeta-Darshan from 30 March, and the first English series there is My Way The Way of White Clouds from 10 May. On 1 December the talks move into Chuang Tzu Auditorium.

heading: A discourse every morning
lede: The whole year is at Chuang Tzu Auditorium, Poona, with a morning discourse almost every day in alternating Hindi and English series of about ten days each. The first darshan diary listed, Hammer on the Rock, begins on 10 December.

heading: Discourses and darshan diaries
lede: A morning discourse and an evening darshan nearly every day in Poona. The darshans are listed under thirteen diaries, from Above All Don't Wobble in January to Blessed Are the Ignorant in December.

heading: Buddha Hall opens
lede: The same daily pattern in Poona. Two Hindi talks in March are listed at an unfinished Buddha Hall, and from 11 April the English series move there, beginning with The First Principle. Darshans stay in Chuang Tzu Auditorium.

heading: Sufis, Tao and Bhakti
lede: Morning series in Buddha Hall and Chuang Tzu Auditorium, with evening darshans all year. Series include Athato Bhakti Jigyasa, The Wisdom of the Sands, The Secret of Secrets and Philosophia Perennis. The wiki lists nothing for 3 to 6 May.

heading: The Dhammapada begins
lede: The Dhammapada starts on 21 June and runs to eight volumes alongside the Hindi series. The wiki lists no talks from 19 November to 4 December.

heading: Two sessions a day
lede: Every entry is in Poona: morning series in Buddha Hall, alternating Hindi and English, and evening darshans published as one diary a month.

heading: Silence, then America
lede: Discourses and darshans continue in Poona until 24 March. A silent period is announced on 21 April, followed by daily silent satsangs in May. He leaves Poona on 31 May, reaches Chidvilas in New Jersey on 2 June and moves to the ranch in Oregon on 29 August. Three books are dictated there from November.

heading: The silent period
lede: No discourses. The wiki lists silent satsangs at Rajneeshpuram, including the First Annual World Celebration in July, and four interviews.

heading: A year of silence
lede: No discourses. Silent satsangs are held at Rajneeshpuram on the four celebration days, including the Second Annual World Celebration in July. Three interviews are dated by year only.

photo.alt: A valley filled with rows of tents and large striped marquees
photo.caption: Rajneeshpuram during the summer festival of 1983.
photo.author: Samvado Gunnar Kossatz

heading: He speaks again
lede: Silent satsangs continue until autumn. On 30 October, evening discourses in English begin at Lao Tzu Grove, Rajneeshpuram, with From Unconsciousness to Consciousness.

heading: Rajneeshpuram to Manali
lede: Evening discourses at Lao Tzu Grove run into early April. Morning discourses resume at Rajneesh Mandir on 30 June, with evening press interviews from 17 July. He leaves Rajneeshpuram on 27 October, is arrested at Charlotte the next day, leaves the United States on 14 November and reaches Manali on 17 November.

photo.alt: A river running through a wooded mountain valley
photo.caption: The Beas river in the Kullu valley near Manali, where he stayed at Span Resort from November.
photo.author: Vyacheslav Argenberg

heading: The world tour
lede: Two talks at Manali on 1 January, then Kathmandu until 14 February and Agios Nikolaos in Crete until 5 March, ending with his arrest. After refused entries across Europe he speaks at Punta del Este in Uruguay from 12 April to 18 June. The wiki lists no talks in Ireland, Jamaica or Portugal. From 31 July he speaks at Sumila in Juhu, Bombay.

photo.alt: A large white stupa with painted eyes and strings of prayer flags
photo.caption: Boudhanath stupa, Kathmandu. He spoke at the Oberoi Soaltee Hotel in the city from 3 January to 14 February.
photo.author: Bernard Gagnon

heading: Return to Poona
lede: He returns to the Poona ashram on 3 January and speaks from 8 January in Chuang Tzu Auditorium, moving to Gautam the Buddha Auditorium during the year. All talks are in English.

heading: Mantra series, then Zen
lede: Every talk is at Gautam the Buddha Auditorium. The year runs from Hari Om Tat Sat and The Mystic Rose into the Zen series, which begin with Live Zen on 22 April.

heading: The last discourses
lede: Short Zen series continue until The Zen Manifesto. Its last talk, on 10 April, is linked on the wiki as his last discourse. Silent satsangs follow, daily from 17 September.

heading: The final satsangs
lede: A silent satsang every evening from 1 to 18 January at Gautam the Buddha Auditorium. The wiki records that Osho leaves his body on 19 January.
